tools.name: get_drives
tools.title: Get Drives
tools.description: Returns raw DriveExpert drive records for the signed-in dealership within a date range, most recent first, paged. Use it to answer questions about drives such as counts, trends, rankings, active vs completed, per-vehicle or per-staff breakdowns, fuel/odometer, and damage. Every drive in the range is returned; a null drive_end_timestamp means the drive is still out. Each row: drive_id, drive_status, drive_type, drive_start_timestamp/drive_end_timestamp, expected_return_timestamp, drive_duration_minutes, vehicle (make/model/year/variant/colour/VIN/stock + damage flags), kilometer & fuel in/out, staff_full_name (the salesperson who ran the drive), driver_count, excess-reduction amount/fee, and drive_link (a direct dashboard URL for the drive). Customer/driver identity (name, contact details, date of birth, address) and the plate/rego are never returned - if the user asks who was driving, give them the drive_link to view the drive in the dashboard. Use the rego filter to find a specific car. REQUIRED: date_from, date_to. Optional: drive_type, rego (plate search), limit (default 100, max 500), offset (default 0 = first page). When has_more is true, call again with offset = next_offset.

limit.description: Optional page size (rows per call), max 500. Defaults to 100 if omitted.

offset.description: Optional row offset for paging. Omit (or 0) for the first page, then pass next_offset from the previous response.

drive_type.description: Optional array of drive types to include (pass one or many). ATD = accompanied test drive, UATD = unaccompanied test drive, LC = loan car, SD = staff drive. Test drives = ["ATD","UATD"]. Omit to include all types. NOTE: filter by these CODES, but in the response drive_type is the full label (e.g. "Accompanied Test Drive").

rego.description: Optional. Find drives for a specific vehicle by plate/rego (exact, case- and space-insensitive).

tools.name: get_bookings
tools.title: Get Bookings
tools.description: Returns raw DriveExpert booking records for the signed-in dealership within a date range, paged. Use it to answer questions about bookings such as counts by status/source/type, made-vs-scheduled timing, and the conversion funnel. Each row: booking_id, status, source, drive_type, created_at (when the booking was made), booking_date (the appointment), checked_in_at / converted_at / cancelled_at, vehicle make/model/year, staff_full_name and drive_id. Customer identity and contact details are never returned. Funnel: pending -> checked_in -> drive_created (booking converted into a drive). date_from and date_to are REQUIRED. Choose which date they bound with date_field: "created_at" (default) or "booking_date" (the scheduled appointment). Paged: if has_more is true, call again with offset = next_offset.

date_field.description: Which date the range bounds: created_at (booking made, default) or booking_date (appointment).

status.description: Optional booking status. Funnel: pending -> checked_in -> drive_created. (Deleted bookings are already excluded.)

source.description: Optional booking source (free text, exact case-insensitive match). Known values: web_dashboard (staff-created), website_widget (public site), mobile_app (mobile app) - but the field is open-ended, so other values may exist.

drive_type.description: Optional array of drive types to include (pass one or many). ATD = accompanied test drive, UATD = unaccompanied test drive, TD = test drive (legacy), LC = loan car. Test drives = ["ATD","UATD","TD"]. Omit to include all types. NOTE: filter by these CODES, but in the response drive_type is the full label (e.g. "Loan Car").

limit.description: Page size (rows per call). Default 100, max 500.

offset.description: Row offset for paging; pass next_offset from the previous response to get the next page.

tools.name: get_evaluations
tools.title: Get Evaluations
tools.description: Runs a structured query over the signed-in user's vehicle evaluations (trade-in appraisals) and returns either raw evaluation rows or aggregated results. This ONE tool answers any evaluation question - listings, counts, trends, averages, breakdowns, summaries - by composing filters, group_by and aggregations; do NOT page through raw rows to compute something BigQuery can aggregate for you. SCOPE: visibility is resolved server-side from the token and matches the web dashboard exactly - a sales executive sees only their own evals, a dealership manager the whole dealership, a group manager every dealership in the group. Shared-copy, incomplete and deleted evals are always excluded. Never ask the user for dealer or user IDs to scope access. MODES: (1) rows - omit group_by/aggregations to get evaluation rows (optionally pick columns with select; default sort EntryDate desc, limit default 100 max 500). (2) aggregate - provide group_by and/or aggregations; results are computed in the database (limit default 200 max 1000 groups). group_by entries are field names, or {field, bucket} for calendar bucketing of timestamp fields (bucket alias is e.g. EntryDate_month; set timezone, an IANA name, for local-day boundaries - default UTC). FIELD NOTES: EntryDate = when the eval was created (UTC). status is TRADED, PURCHASED, PENDING, LOST_SOLD_ELSEWHERE, LOST_CUSTOMER_KEEPING, LOST_NOT_PURCHASING_FROM_US or LOST_NOT_BUYING_ANYMORE (often null = no outcome yet); tradedFlag/tradedAt also mark traded outcomes. FinalPrice = appraised price (null/0 = not priced yet); timeToPrice = seconds from creation to pricing. KM = odometer. Make/Model/Variant come from VIN decoding; dashboardMakeValue/dashboardModelValue are the normalized names the dashboard charts use - prefer them for make/model breakdowns. source = how the eval was created (WEBSITE, APP, API, LINKS, DEALERCELL, MOTORMERCHANTS, AH-SERVICE, AH-WEB, AH-OTHER, AH-LINK, BULK). acquisitionType = e.g. AUCTION, TRADE_IN, DIRECT_PURCHASE, SERVICE_LOAN or a dealer-custom label. userName/dealerName identify which staff member created the eval and where (there are no ID fields). The selling customer's identity and contact details are never available; customerState is the only customer field, for regional breakdowns. Registration and VIN are returned only when listed in select - include them only when the user asks for a specific car or its plate/VIN. Timestamp fields: EntryDate, completedAt, pricedAt, kmUpdatedAt, tradedLogAt, tradedAt, tradedDateChanged, listedAt, mmDateAccepted, mmDateTransacted, mmTransactionCancelled. ERRORS: if the response contains query_error, the query was invalid - fix it per the message and retry. Paged: if has_more is true, call again with offset = next_offset.

filters.description: Optional AND-combined filters (max 20). Use an EntryDate filter to bound the time window whenever the question implies one.

op.description: Comparison operator. contains/starts_with are case-insensitive and only for string fields.

value.description: Comparison value. Array of 2 for between ([min, max]); array for in/not_in; omit for is_null/is_not_null. Timestamp values are date/time strings like "2026-01-31" or "2026-01-31T23:59:59Z" (UTC).

select.description: Rows mode only: columns to return - pick only the columns the question needs. Omit for the default set (ID, EntryDate, userName, dealerName, Make, Model, Variant, Year, KM, FinalPrice, status, source, acquisitionType, tradedAt).

group_by.description: Aggregate mode: dimensions (max 5). Field names, or {field, bucket} to bucket a timestamp field by day/week/month/quarter/year.

field.description: A timestamp field to bucket, e.g. EntryDate.

aggregations.description: Aggregate mode: metrics (max 10). Defaults to a single count when group_by is set. Output name defaults to fn_field (e.g. avg_FinalPrice) or count.

field.description: Field to aggregate. Required for every fn except count. sum/avg need a numeric field; min/max accept numeric or timestamp.

order_by.description: Sort order (max 3). Defaults: rows -> EntryDate desc; aggregate -> first metric desc.

field.description: Row queries: any queryable field. Aggregate queries: a group_by field name, a bucket alias like EntryDate_month, or an aggregation output name like count or avg_FinalPrice.

limit.description: Max results per page. Rows: default 100, max 500. Aggregate: default 200, max 1000.

offset.description: Paging offset - pass next_offset from the previous response when has_more is true.

timezone.description: IANA timezone (e.g. "Australia/Brisbane") for calendar bucketing of timestamps. Default UTC.

tools.name: create_evaluation
tools.title: Create Evaluation
tools.description: Creates a vehicle evaluation (trade-in appraisal) for the signed-in user through a strict three-step flow. Call this tool SEQUENTIALLY, one step per call, echoing back the flow_state returned by the previous call. Each response says whether to stay on the step (fix something / ask the user) or advance. STEP 1 "identify_vehicle": provide vin, or rego + state (read them from the user's images or message; VIN takes priority when both are available; NEVER guess or invent them - if neither is available, ask the user before calling). Returns the decoded vehicle details. STEP 2 "confirm": show the vehicle details to the user, get an explicit yes, then call with user_confirmed=true. STEP 3 "complete": submit eval_details - fill ONLY what is actually known, omit the rest; km is strongly recommended. customer_details is the person selling/trading the vehicle to the dealership. Its name/phone/email/address fields must belong to that person, parsed when clearly identified (trade-in paperwork, ID, or stated by the user) - NEVER a dealership/business/lister from a vehicle advertisement. Its suburb/state/postcode fields may be filled from the vehicle's location in the source even when the seller is not named. This finalizes the evaluation. The flow_state blob is signed - pass it back EXACTLY as received. If it is rejected, restart from identify_vehicle. Photo upload is not supported here - tell the user to add photos via the dashboard or mobile app afterwards.

step.description: Which step of the flow to execute.

rego.description: identify_vehicle: the number plate, used with state when no VIN is available.

state.description: identify_vehicle: the rego's registration state, e.g. QLD, NSW, SA.

user_confirmed.description: confirm: true only after the user explicitly confirmed the decoded vehicle.

flow_state.description: The signed state blob from the previous step's response, echoed back verbatim. Required for confirm and complete.

eval_details.description: complete: vehicle/evaluation details. Fill only what is known.

condition.description: Overall condition rating as an integer from 0 to 10 (send 7, not "7/10").

acquisition_type.description: How the car is being acquired: AUCTION, TRADE_IN, DIRECT_PURCHASE, SERVICE_LOAN, HEAD_OFFICE, EX_FLEET, EX_LEASE, BUY_BACK, or a dealer-custom label.

service_history.description: Service history: 0=No, 1=Yes, 2=Missing book/no history, 3=Partial, 4=Full non-genuine, 5=Full genuine, 6=Full mixed.

total_loss.description: Has been declared a total loss / write-off.

financed.description: Money still owing on the vehicle.

build_date.description: Build date as "month/year", e.g. "6/2020". Applies to this evaluation only.

first_registered.description: First registration date, e.g. "15/03/2021", "3/2021", or "1 Mar 2021".

variant.description: Corrected variant/badge if the decoded variant shown at the confirm step was wrong. Applies to this evaluation only.

recon.description: Reconditioning costs, protection products, and service/warranty dates. IMPORTANT: provide every known value in ONE call - partial recon objects across retries overwrite earlier values.

tyres.description: Tyres cost (excluded from the recon total by design).

customer_details.description: complete: the selling customer. name/phone/email/address only for a clearly identified selling person (never a dealership/business/lister from an ad); suburb/state/postcode may come from the vehicle's location in the source. Omit fields that are unknown.

name.description: Full name of the person selling the vehicle. Never a business or dealership name.

suburb.description: Suburb / city - the seller's if known, else the vehicle's location.

state.description: State - the seller's if known, else the vehicle's location.

postcode.description: Postcode - the seller's if known, else the vehicle's location.

custom_fields.description: Values for dealer-configured custom fields, as key/value pairs matching the dealer's existing field names exactly (e.g. {"Lead Source": "Walk-in"}). Names not configured for this dealer are ignored by the server.

tools.name: create_bulk_evaluations
tools.title: Create Bulk Evaluations
tools.description: Creates vehicle evaluations in bulk from data shared in the conversation (pasted rows or a file you can read). The users are business people: always talk to them in plain business language - say "vehicles", never rows/records/columns/fields, and only ever mention details that apply to them. Follow this workflow IN ORDER before calling: STEP 1 - MAP: convert the source data into the template columns reg, state, vin, km, notes, acquisitionType, whatever the original column names or order (rego/plate/registration -> reg; mileage/odometer/miles -> km; source/acquisition -> acquisitionType; notes is optional and becomes an evaluation note). NEVER fill notes with your own assumptions: if the source has extra details that could be worth keeping as a note, suggest that to the user with one example vehicle and ask. If they confirm, use it; if they decline, leave notes empty; or they can tell you what to put instead. STEP 2 - IDENTIFY: required details depend on the account's region, which the server resolves and enforces - AUS and US: a rego/plate together with its state, or a VIN - plus the kilometres/mileage; GCC: a VIN plus the kilometres. notes and acquisition type are always optional. By default tell the user how many vehicles are missing required details (with a couple of examples) - those cannot be imported. Only ever mention details that exist in the user's region (GCC has no rego or state). STEP 3 - SUMMARIZE: show the user a short summary of the importable vehicles with a few aggregations that help them decide what to import - e.g. total vehicles, counts by state and by acquisition type (where relevant), kilometres/mileage range, duplicates. Ask whether they want to leave anything out or create evaluations for all of them. STEP 4 - ACTION: after they confirm the set, ask how to handle cars that already have an evaluation (existing_eval_action). STEP 5 - IMPORT: call the tool with the final rows, existing_eval_action and user_confirmed=true. Each call imports at most 1000 vehicles. If the confirmed set is larger, import the first 1000, report the outcome, then ask the user whether to continue with the next chunk and repeat until done or they stop. Only chunk AFTER the user confirmed the set - leaving vehicles out may shrink it below the cap. The result includes the outcome to report back.

notes.description: Optional note created on the evaluation. Only content the user explicitly approved or dictated - never your own assumption; omit otherwise.

acquisitionType.description: How the car is being acquired, e.g. TRADE_IN, AUCTION.

rows.description: The final mapped vehicles to import (max 1000 per call; chunk larger confirmed sets). Every vehicle needs its region's required details - leave out those missing any of it.

existing_eval_action.description: What to do when an evaluation already exists for the same car. new-eval = create a new one; "regardless of existing Eval age" = update KM on the existing one; update-30 / update-90 = update KM only if the existing eval is younger than 30/90 days. Ask the user which they want - do not pick silently.

user_confirmed.description: true only after the user saw the summary/aggregations of the mapped data and explicitly confirmed which records to import.

existing_eval_action.description: What to do when an evaluation already exists for the same car. new-eval = create a new one; "regardless of existing Eval age" = update KM on the existing one; update-30 / update-90 = update KM only if the existing eval is younger than 30/90 days. Ask the user which they want - do not pick silently.

user_confirmed.description: true only after the user saw the summary/aggregations of the mapped data and explicitly confirmed which records to import.

flags.description: Creates a vehicle evaluation (trade-in appraisal) for the signed-in user through a strict three-step flow. Call this tool SEQUENTIALLY, one step per call, echoing back the flow_state returned by the previous call. Each response says whether to stay on the step (fix something / ask the user) or advance. STEP 1 "identify_vehicle": provide vin, or rego + state (read them from the user's images or message; VIN takes priority when both are available; NEVER guess or invent them - if neither is available, ask the user before calling). Returns the decoded vehicle details. STEP 2 "confirm": show the vehicle details to the user, get an explicit yes, then call with user_confirmed=true. STEP 3 "complete": submit eval_details - fill ONLY what is actually known, omit the rest; km is strongly recommended. customer_details is the person selling/trading the vehicle to the dealership. Its name/phone/email/address fields must belong to that person, parsed when clearly identified (trade-in paperwork, ID, or stated by the user) - NEVER a dealership/business/lister from a vehicle advertisement. Its suburb/state/postcode fields may be filled from the vehicle's location in the source even when the seller is not named. This finalizes the evaluation. The flow_state blob is signed - pass it back EXACTLY as received. If it is rejected, restart from identify_vehicle. Photo upload is not supported here - tell the user to add photos via the dashboard or mobile app afterwards.
flags.hypothesis: Broad language may route a narrow task to an unnecessarily large response; bounded semantics may explain this language.

flags.description: Creates vehicle evaluations in bulk from data shared in the conversation (pasted rows or a file you can read). The users are business people: always talk to them in plain business language - say "vehicles", never rows/records/columns/fields, and only ever mention details that apply to them. Follow this workflow IN ORDER before calling: STEP 1 - MAP: convert the source data into the template columns reg, state, vin, km, notes, acquisitionType, whatever the original column names or order (rego/plate/registration -> reg; mileage/odometer/miles -> km; source/acquisition -> acquisitionType; notes is optional and becomes an evaluation note). NEVER fill notes with your own assumptions: if the source has extra details that could be worth keeping as a note, suggest that to the user with one example vehicle and ask. If they confirm, use it; if they decline, leave notes empty; or they can tell you what to put instead. STEP 2 - IDENTIFY: required details depend on the account's region, which the server resolves and enforces - AUS and US: a rego/plate together with its state, or a VIN - plus the kilometres/mileage; GCC: a VIN plus the kilometres. notes and acquisition type are always optional. By default tell the user how many vehicles are missing required details (with a couple of examples) - those cannot be imported. Only ever mention details that exist in the user's region (GCC has no rego or state). STEP 3 - SUMMARIZE: show the user a short summary of the importable vehicles with a few aggregations that help them decide what to import - e.g. total vehicles, counts by state and by acquisition type (where relevant), kilometres/mileage range, duplicates. Ask whether they want to leave anything out or create evaluations for all of them. STEP 4 - ACTION: after they confirm the set, ask how to handle cars that already have an evaluation (existing_eval_action). STEP 5 - IMPORT: call the tool with the final rows, existing_eval_action and user_confirmed=true. Each call imports at most 1000 vehicles. If the confirmed set is larger, import the first 1000, report the outcome, then ask the user whether to continue with the next chunk and repeat until done or they stop. Only chunk AFTER the user confirmed the set - leaving vehicles out may shrink it below the cap. The result includes the outcome to report back.
